name: PUSH TO CLOUD — store-and-forward to farm-ingest
info:
The phone is behind carrier CGNAT, so nothing can dial IN to it. This group
dials OUT instead: readings are buffered in flow context and POSTed in batches
to the VPS. Survives 4G dropouts — nothing is deleted from the buffer until
the server has answered 200.

**Change the URL or token in the `drain outbox` function** — both live at the
top of that one node, nowhere else.

Both `http in` nodes feed `queue for cloud` directly rather than going through
the `store …` functions, because those return null on `ok:false` and the fault
rows are the ones you most want off the phone.

The push is EVENT-DRIVEN: every arriving reading triggers a drain. Android
freezes Termux's JS timers when the phone dozes, so a purely scheduled push
silently stops while everything still looks healthy. An ESP POST has already
woken the process, so draining on that event needs no wake-lock. The 30 s
inject is only a backstop for retrying while no new readings are arriving.

⚠️ The buffer lives in memory. A Node-RED restart drops whatever is queued.
To survive restarts, add a filesystem context store in settings.js.
